__comment: Chain ingestion rules. A chain reacts to a committed write on trigger_table and projects it onto target_table through a mapper. | The production->inventory rule was removed with the demo tables it referenced (2026-08-01 fixture reset).

rules.__comment: dt_log -> dt_map: the DT map is DERIVED. dt_log is the record; the map is a projection of it, so nothing should ever write dt_map by hand -- a replay would then silently disagree with the hand-written rows. | SHIPS DISABLED and stays disabled this round by instruction. What was measured (2026-08-01): a chain CAN address a single map cell -- crud.apply_batch_updates composes the composite business key from the update payload itself (crud.py:1051-1059) when the caller omits business_key_val and supplies every composite_key_source column, and dt_map's composite key includes dt_x/dt_y, so one business key = one cell. What a chain CANNOT do is PURGE: replace_map lives on the batch (schemas.py:138) and chain_ingestion_worker.py:437-441 constructs the batch itself and never sets it, so a chain can only upsert cells and never delete stale ones. That is the open question, and it is why this stays off.
rules.name: dt_log_to_dt_map

rules.__comment: DT frame metadata: the source map is dt_log itself, one metadata row per dt_job. The mapper calls the same read-only alignment-view service as the UI, accepts only a declared index-axis winner, and writes the full projected grid_metadata through normal chain priority (so user metadata remains higher priority). dt_job ingestion is one transaction, hence this batch trigger sees the completed job; incomplete decision keys are intentionally a no-op. dt_map is NOT the target here: it is the later standardized projection.
rules.name: dt_log_to_dt_alignment_metadata

rules.__comment: S2 identity projection. This is the explicitly allowed second hop of dt_log -> wafer_map_metadata -> dt_inventory. The worker keeps all other chain-created events blocked; allow_chain_trigger is safe only because the loader rejects cycles among such edges.
rules.name: dt_metadata_to_dt_inventory

rules.__comment: S3: dt_inventory carries the confirmed dt_frame and its derived portable X/Y/sign/offset equation. Project matching dt_log rows into the standard-coordinate dt_map. Each batch replaces exactly one dt_job map, never an inferred lot/slot map.
rules.name: dt_inventory_to_standard_dt_map

rules.__comment: Core automatic frame: dt_core_view is review-only and is intentionally NOT in this chain. The mapper reads one completed dt_log job, selects the primary core by the earliest dt_index (stable lot/slot/wafer tie breakers), filters the same raw rows in the shared alignment engine, then atomically writes dt_inventory.core_frame plus core_x/y base/sign/offset equations. All material-specific policy lives below: change reference.table/map_id_template/fields when the physical defect map becomes wafer-id keyed; change accepted_metrics and alignment_thresholds without editing Python. The configured empty index_col forces defect/bin value scoring instead of transfer-order scoring.
rules.name: dt_log_to_primary_core_frame

rules.__comment: Usage overlay refresh after a core frame/equation update. The output is its own derived table and replaces exactly one enriched core_wafer map. This is the allowed second hop from the automatic core-frame chain.
rules.name: dt_inventory_to_core_usage_map

rules.__comment: Usage overlay revisit after raw ingest or enrichment fills core_wafer. lot/slot-only rows are intentionally a no-op; when enrichment writes core_wafer the same rule rebuilds that wafer's complete usage footprint.
rules.name: dt_log_to_core_usage_map

rules.__comment: [NOT fixture data -- DO NOT DELETE AS DEAD] This table is not referenced by any fixture, so it looks unused. It is not. It exists because it is the only live exercise of the CHAIN path: test_api.py::test_chained_ingestion asserts on the outbox events the production_plan -> inventory_master chain produces, and removing these declarations silently removes that coverage. The dt_log_to_dt_map fixture chain cannot replace it -- that rule ships enabled:false on purpose (a chain can upsert map cells but cannot purge them), and turning an unsafe rule on to keep a test green is the same mistake as deleting the test. Its auto-update collector is disabled, so the table is declared but never grows. | The rule stays ENABLED so the test exercises the real worker path rather than a mock.
rules.name: production_to_inventory_reservation_batch
